newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close up on cash ideas, pork bellies weak.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close up on cash ideas, pork bellies weak.

text.p: Local short covering and light commercial support linked to expectations of a steady-firm cash hog trend next week held CME lean hog futures higher at the close. Pork bellies remained pressured by a weak cash product market, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.750 to 0.200 cent per lb higher with July up most at 84.000 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.875 lower to 0.075 higher with July off most at 82.175 cents.
Expectations of tighter hog marketings next week prompted support in hog futures despite lower cash hog prices Thursday and generally easier wholesale pork prices, traders said.
"Hog (market) numbers just don't seem to be there," one trader said.
Technical follow through was also lacking which prompted talk that the pullback in futures earlier this week now looks like a correction in the market, they added.

Rand Financials remained a notable buyer of August after early selling by R.J. O'Brien. Local short covering added to mixed commission house buying in July. In hog options, First Chicago bought October 72 puts early and Iowa Grain sold August 80 puts late, pit sources said.
Nearby pork belly futures posted closing declines, weighed down by lower cash belly quotes, traders said.

USDA quoted cash bellies down to $84 per cwt on Thursday, a $6 drop from the $90 quoted earlier in the week. The market has a tendency to peak when cash reaches the $90 per cwt area and cuts off user interest, some sources noted.
However, strength in hog futures limited downside potential in the belly pit, sources said.
Prudential Securities notably bought August early but selling by R.J. O'Brien and Rosenthal Collins weighed on prices. R.J. O'Brien bought July, pit sources said.
